1.explanation: Each of these six folders contains the React component implementation (and stories) for the corresponding form element, including its skeleton state markup. By examining the code in these directories you can pinpoint how the skeleton labels are being rendered (empty <label> tags) and modify or extend the markup—e.g. inject placeholder text, add aria-label attributes, or conditionally hide the label element—to resolve the missing-label accessibility violation.
1.bug_scenario: When viewing the “skeleton” (loading placeholder) variants of the Checkbox, NumberInput, Select, Slider, TextArea and TextInput components in the Carbon React library, each component renders a blank <label> element (class="bx--label bx--skeleton") but no visible or descriptive text inside that label. DAP flags each of these empty labels as an accessibility violation (“Provide descriptive text in LABEL elements”) because screen readers have no text to announce for these inputs. The gray placeholder boxes for the inputs themselves are rendered, but their associated labels are empty.
